prompts.text: Age at scan places a participant within a developmental stage.
Developmental stage provides context for population-level measurements.
Sex category records demographic composition without defining diagnosis.
Age-group encoding summarizes participant age at assessment.
Acquisition site records the center where a scan was collected.
Multisite cohorts can differ in scanner setup and acquisition conditions.
prompts.feature_basis: One-hot SITE_ID categories; collection context only.

prompts.text: Site categories describe data collection context, not a clinical finding.
Participant background may vary across centers and age distributions.
Anatomical contrast-to-noise summarizes tissue signal separation.
Signal-to-noise reflects image signal relative to background noise.
Foreground-to-background energy ratio summarizes image intensity distribution.
Structural image quality metrics describe contrast and signal clarity.
Entropy focus criterion measures intensity distribution and image disorder.
Full width at half maximum summarizes image smoothness and blurring.
Quality index captures artifacts in structural MRI image intensity.
Image artifact measures characterize acquisition and preprocessing quality.
Framewise displacement summarizes head movement between volumes.
Mean framewise displacement captures average motion during an fMRI scan.
Outlier fraction describes volumes flagged for motion-related artifacts.
DVARS tracks signal changes between consecutive image volumes.
Functional contrast-to-noise metrics summarize image signal distribution.
Temporal signal fluctuations can affect measured functional connectivity.
prompts.feature_basis: func_dvars and func_quality; measurement context only.

prompts.text: Global signal regression records a functional preprocessing characteristic.
Functional scan quality measures characterize noise and motion artifacts.
Resting-state BOLD correlations summarize pairwise signal covariation.
Functional connections reflect dependence between regional time series.
Correlation strength describes synchronized BOLD fluctuations across regions.
Selected connectivity edges encode pairwise resting-state network relationships.
prompts.feature_basis: 256 RFE-selected features from the upper triangle of 111-region correlation matrices; exact edge identities were not retained.

prompts.text: Brain networks coordinate distributed activity through functional connections.
prompts.feature_basis: Network-level interpretation of selected rs-fMRI edges.

prompts.text: Long-range connectivity links activity across separated brain regions.
prompts.feature_basis: General functional-connectivity concept; no selected edge identity is asserted.

prompts.text: Network patterns summarize interactions across multiple brain systems.
prompts.feature_basis: Network-level interpretation of selected rs-fMRI edges.

prompts.text: Connectivity profiles capture distributed organization without a single-region label.
prompts.feature_basis: 256 selected edge values have no retained ROI-pair identifiers.

prompts: Autism spectrum disorder is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition involving differences in social communication and restricted or repetitive behaviors.
Autism spectrum disorder has been associated with heterogeneous resting-state functional connectivity patterns rather than one universal abnormal connection.
Studies of autism report variable interactions involving default mode, salience, and executive-control networks across individuals and cohorts.
Autism research reports diverse functional connectivity patterns in sensory, attention, and social-processing networks, with changes varying across people.
Typically developing individuals show diverse age-related social communication and behavioral development without an autism spectrum diagnosis.
Typical development involves heterogeneous resting-state functional connectivity patterns rather than one universal reference connection.
Typical development includes age-dependent interactions among default mode, salience, and executive-control networks across individuals.
Typical development includes variable functional connectivity patterns in sensory, attention, and social-processing networks across people.

ADHD.source: disease-mismatch control; not an ADHD task
prompts: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition involving differences in attention, impulsivity, and activity regulation.
Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder has been associated with heterogeneous resting-state functional connectivity patterns rather than one universal abnormal connection.
Studies of ADHD report variable interactions involving default mode, salience, and executive-control networks across individuals and cohorts.
ADHD research reports diverse functional connectivity patterns in sensory, attention, and executive-control networks, with changes varying across people.
A technical MRI record describes structural image contrast and noise estimates.
The imaging record summarizes structural signal quality and image artifacts.
This technical description concerns scanner settings and anatomical image properties.
The record contains structural imaging measurements obtained during preprocessing.
A technical MRI record describes functional image motion and temporal signal variation.
The imaging record summarizes functional signal quality and movement artifacts.
This technical description concerns fMRI preprocessing and temporal image properties.
The record contains functional imaging measurements obtained during preprocessing.

design_notes.label_mapping: Raw DX_GROUP 1=ASD and 2=TD; main.py subtracts one, giving model labels 0=ASD and 1=TD.
design_notes.medical_scope: Prompts are cautious group-level background statements, not individual diagnostic rules or universal biomarkers.
design_notes.pheno_scope: No participant-specific cognition or psychometric values are available; none are fabricated.
design_notes.freeze_rule: All text is fixed before training and is never edited from test results.
